hook.line: Every good story has two layers: the scene (late, raining, nobody around) and the things that happen in it. You already know both pasts. Now you get to use them together, and Spanish gives each layer its own one.
hook.es: Era tarde y llovía. De repente se fue la luz.
hook.en: It was late and it was raining. Suddenly the power went out.

rule:
English has one past: *was*, *lived*, *went*. Spanish has two, and your English won't tell you which one you need. It depends on how you're telling it.

The event past says it happened: start to finish, done, one item in the story.
The describing past puts you in the middle: it was going on, or that's how life was back then, with no end in view.

*Llovía cuando llegué.* It was raining when I arrived.
*Llovió toda la noche.* It rained all night.
*Rosa cerraba el café a las seis.* Rosa used to close the café at six.
*Anoche Tomás cerró el café a las diez.* Last night Tomás closed the café at ten.
*Comía a las dos.* I used to eat at two.
*Comí a las dos.* I ate at two.

It isn't about how long it lasted. Forty years can be one item: *Hernando fue taxista cuarenta años.* One second can be the scene: *Yo salía cuando sonó el teléfono.*

**The test.** First, try *was doing* or *used to do* in your English. If it still says what you mean, use the describing past. It was raining: yes, *llovía*. I went to the beach every year: I used to go, yes, *iba*.

If not, try *and then* in front. And then the phone rang works: event past, *sonó*. And then it was late sounds wrong: describing past, *era tarde*.

A length or a total usually wraps it up, so it's the event past: *toda la noche*, *diez años*, *tres veces*.

**The traps.** Time words don't decide. *Ayer* goes with both: *Ayer fui al banco. Ayer llovía cuando salí.* Length doesn't decide. And *used to* is not *usar*: the ending does that job, *vivía*.

Sometimes both are right, and you're only choosing how to tell it: *¿Cómo fue tu niñez?* and *¿Cómo era tu niñez?*

One more thing. The event past draws a line around a state, and with some verbs that line is the moment it started. *Sabía la verdad*: I knew the truth. *Supe la verdad*: I found out the truth. *Conocía a Vale*: I knew Vale. *Conocí a Vale*: I met Vale.
smallPrint: Teachers call the scene past the imperfect (*pretérito imperfecto*) and the event past the preterite (*pretérito indefinido*).

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ tarde y llovía.* (*Fue* or *Era*) It was late and it was raining.
yourTurn.why: The time is part of the scene, so *era*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *De repente ___ la luz.* (*se iba* or *se fue*) Suddenly the power went out.
yourTurn.answer: De repente se fue la luz.
yourTurn.why: *De repente* brings in something that happened, so the event past *se fue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Eran las diez cuando ___ el teléfono.* (*sonaba* or *sonó*) It was ten o'clock when the phone rang.
yourTurn.answer: Eran las diez cuando sonó el teléfono.
yourTurn.why: The ring is the event that lands in the scene: *sonó*.

yourTurn.prompt: It was eleven o'clock and there was nobody in the street.
yourTurn.answer: Eran las once y no había nadie en la calle.
yourTurn.why: The time and what there was are both scene: *eran*, *había*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Where were you when the power went out?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Dónde estabas cuando se fue la luz?
yourTurn.why: Where you were is the scene (*estabas*); the power cut is the event (*se fue*).

yourTurn.prompt: I opened the door and there was nobody there.
yourTurn.answer: Abrí la puerta y no había nadie.
accept: Abrí la puerta y no había nadie ahí.
Abrí la puerta y no había nadie allí.
yourTurn.why: Opening the door is an event, *abrí*; the empty doorway is the scene, *había*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into a story about the past: *Llueve cuando llego.*
yourTurn.why: The rain was already going on, so *llovía*; arriving is the event, so *llegué*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into a story about the past: *Estoy en la cocina y suena el teléfono.*
yourTurn.answer: Estaba en la cocina y sonó el teléfono.
accept: Yo estaba en la cocina y sonó el teléfono.
yourTurn.why: Where you were is the scene, *estaba*; the phone is the event, *sonó*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The time and the weather set the scene, so both take the describing past.

pitfalls.wrong: De repente se iba la luz.
pitfalls.right: De repente se fue la luz.
pitfalls.why: *De repente* means something happened, so use the event past *se fue*.

pitfalls.wrong: Tomás tuvo siete años cuando se fue a Toronto.
pitfalls.right: Tomás tenía siete años cuando se fue a Toronto.
pitfalls.why: Age in a story is part of the scene: *tenía*.
How someone felt is scene, and feelings use *estar*: *estaba*.

personal: Think of a night something surprising happened to you. Write two lines of scene (*era*, *estaba*, *había*, *llovía*) and then one event that starts with *De repente*.
